title: automate-kms-hsm-tls-rotation-private-installer-helm-terraform
author: Samira Patel
release_notes: Add automated KMS/HSM key rotation and TLS certificate rotation for Private Installer. Updates Helm charts and Terraform modules to support managed rotation, optional Vault and Sealed Secrets integration, and safe upgrade/rollback paths.
description: Motivation: Customers running Redwood Private require automated rotation of TLS certificates and KMS/HSM keys for compliance and operational hygiene. Currently rotations are manual and error-prone during upgrades. This PR adds end-to-end automation for key and cert rotation using a controller + CRDs, Helm chart flags, and Terraform module changes. Summary of changes: - Controller: new rotation-controller (go) that watches RotationPolicy CR and orchestrates HSM/KMS key rotation, cert issuance via cert-manager or Vault, and triggers sealed-secrets re-encryption when using SealedSecrets. - CRDs: RotationPolicy (spec: target, rotationWindow, gracePeriod, backend{aws_kms|vault_hsm|gcp_kms}, keyAlias, certRequest). - Helm: values to opt-in to automated rotation, templates for rotation controller deployment, service account RBAC, and helper hooks for safe pre-upgrade checks. - Terraform: add rotation module (redwood_rotation) to create KMS aliases, HSM policies, and optional Vault roles; outputs to feed private-installer values. - Migration/Upgrade: add upgrade hook that validates current keys/certs, creates a safe rotation plan, and supports canary rotations (subset of namespaces). - Rollback: controller records rotation state and can rollback to previous key/cert via previousSecretRef if rotation fails. - Sealed Secrets & Vault: support for re-wrapping sealed secrets via kubeseal with new key and support for Vault transit re-encryption path. - Tests: unit tests, helm lint, terraform validate, and an e2e job that runs a dry-run plan against a kind cluster with a mocked HSM and Vault. Checklist: [x] Rotation controller implementation [x] CRD and CR samples [x] Helm templates and values.yaml docs [x] Terraform module and example usage [x] Integration tests and CI jobs [x] Docs/upgrade notes [x] Security review Notes: - The default is opt-in. Admins must enable rotation by setting values.rotation.enabled=true and choose a backend. - HSM support requires PKCS#11 config supplied via secret mounted with restricted RBAC. - Vault path and policies are configured via Terraform outputs or Helm values. - We intentionally rotate keys in a way that preserves old key material for a configurable grace period (default 7 days) to allow rollback and verify consumers updated their cached KVs. - This PR touches stateful areas; please follow upgrade notes when applying to production clusters. Related Linear: ENG-6413 (rotation controller), ENG-6531 (helm/terraform integration).

notes: Upgrade steps: 1) terraform apply rotation module in infra account to provision aliases/roles 2) set helm values.rotation.enabled=true and provide backend config 3) apply helm upgrade with --wait and monitor rotation-controller logs 4) validate service endpoints and key/cert versions
Rollback: controller keeps previousSecretRef and previousKeyAlias for configurable gracePeriod; use scripts/rollback/restore-previous-key.sh to restore if automated rollback fails
Security: secrets used for PKCS#11 or Vault are mounted with read-only file permissions and the controller follows least-privilege SA; HSM private keys never leave HSM

Notes on compatibility: AWS KMS uses alias re-pointing; GCP KMS rotates by creating new CryptoKeyVersion and updating references; Vault uses transit rewrap. All backends expose standardized status fields on RotationPolicy CRD.
Testing guidance: run tests/e2e/rotation/dryrun_test.go locally with KIND_CLUSTER=true and set MOCK_HSM=true for faster iteration.
